angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 49,812,120 km at 1978.60 pc = 0.34 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, SV Mon: Baade-Wesselink distance (pc) 1978.6 +/- 95 (Monte-Carlo) (https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.5478): 1978.6 +/- 95 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 0.4324 +/- 0.0321 mas (same row, RUWE 1.01), 13.5 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 71.6 +/- 3.5 solar radii from Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, SV Mon: Baade-Wesselink mean radius (solar radii) 71.6 +/- 3.5 (Monte-Carlo) (https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.5478): 49,812,120 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 5375 +/- 406 K from Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, VizieR J/A+A/635/A33/table1, recno 157, Name='SV Mon', columns Teff, e_Teff (K): Teff 5375 +/- 406 K from a fit to the spectral energy distribution at mean light (not spectroscopic) (https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.02186). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, VizieR J/A+A/635/A33/table1, recno 157, Name='SV Mon', columns Teff, e_Teff (K): Teff 5375 +/- 406 K from a fit to the spectral energy distribution at mean light (not spectroscopic) (https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.02186)
surfaceGravitySource: log g 0.7 from 2023A&A...678A.195D, the median of its 5 spectra; the 12 published values span log g 0.7 to 1.5, across which the limb law changes by at most 1.2% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A%26A...678A.195D)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, V* SV Mon: spectral type G1Ib (2007A&A...469..713M)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, V* SV Mon: main object type cC*, Classical Cepheid Variable

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
